achievements:
1. Represented my state(West Bengal) at the Under-16 level in cricket.

cultureAnswer:
I am an IPM student. When I stepped into the campus 3 years back and I got to know about all the committees, SportsComm is the first committee which really caught my eye. Sports is something which runs through my veins and 3 years back I had made up my mind that during my MBA days, SportsComm is where I want to be. Moving away from professional cricket due to academics has taken a part of my life away from me. I want to relive at least some of it through this committee- not just cricket, but for every single sport. During my IPM days, I have been there for every game of every sport during SPEED to root for my cohort because I respect each and every sports discipline. If I get a chance to be a part of the committee, I would want to promote the sporting culture to the entire campus ensuring equality irrespective of the gender, background, interests etc. My main goal will be to create such a close knit sporting ecosystem such that each and every single individual in this campus should have sports as a part of their daily life- whether it be a recreation, passion or a means to stay fit.

I would be really grateful if I get this opportunity.
favoriteMemory:
1. My best ever memory in sports was when I got selected for my State's Under 16 cricket team. I remembered all the hard work and sacrifices I had made to get into the team and I got really emotional when my discipline had finally paid off.

2. My second best sports memory was the 2022 FIFA World Cup Final. I started watching football because of Lionel Messi when I was very young. From then, I was a Barca and Argentina fan. World Cup is a major trophy which had eluded Leo for several years and after so many heartbreaks, I really wanted 2022 to be the year for the blue and white brigade. The final according to me was the best football match that has ever been played till date. It tested my nerves to the very limits with both teams keeping us on edge for 120 minutes. When Gonzalo Montiel scored the winning penalty for Argentina, I cried tears of joy. I felt that the child in me who started watching the sport because of Leo, had finally watched his idol achieve the greatest feat possible. I don't think any other moment can top that feeling.

achievements:

* Gold - Box Cricket
* Gold-Football
* Silver - Tug-of-war
* Gold - Shotput(Self)

I playbasketball too
cultureAnswer:
"I just don't think that Brooke could've done this. Exercise gives you endorphins. Endorphins make you happy. Happy people just don't shoot their husbands. They just don't." ~ Elle Woods(Leagally Blonde)

Sports, be it any type of a sport, makes me happy. Like it could be a sport that I have never played, I will still have the same level of enthusiasm to learn and play.
favoriteMemory:
After losing two years to COVID, I wanted to make the most of the last Sports Day of my undergraduate years. To set the context, the gender ratio in engineering is very skewed. There were very few girls in the IT department, and even fewer who were interested in sports. We had a couple of tournaments, such as football, cricket, badminton, and more, and being me, I wanted to participate in all of them.

The problem was finding or forming a team. I was part of the main IT department committee, so I sent messages to the unofficial group that included students from all years, requesting interested girls to join the teams. That attempt wasn't very successful. So, I started approaching any and every girl from the IT department I could find and personally tried to convince them to join. After multiple very embarrassing conversations and rejections, people slowly started joining.

I'm very grateful to all the girls who showed up because I would call them for practice in the scorching sun (we didn't really have an option because of the schedule), and they never complained even once.

Short story long, my favorite memory was the tug-of-war tournament. My team was severely underweight. Practically speaking, we had very little chance of even winning the first match. But all our practice came in handy. The techniques and strategies we had worked on helped us overpower the heavier teams. We made it through the quarterfinals and the semifinals.

The final was against the Civil team, our biggest rivals. They were not only skilled players, but they also had the ideal weight advantage. In tug-of-war, each match consists of three rounds, and the team that wins two rounds wins the match. Not going to lie, I was extremely surprised that we managed to win one entire round against them. Although they won the match, I couldn't have been happier with our silver medal.

name: Aaditya Vijaykrishnan
cultureAnswer:
For me, being part of the Sports Committee, means being part of a community that brings people together outside the classrooms and all the academic pressure. Sports have always been a great way to build friendships, build healthy competition, and give people a space to have fun. At a place like TAPMI, I believe the Sports Committee can play an important role in making sure that everyone, regardless of their sporting skills, feels encouraged to participate in sports. 

I would like to contribute by trying to create an environment where sports are not limited to only the professional players. While tournaments and competitions are important, I believe the culture around sports is equally important. I would like to encourage higher participation through events, informal games, and activities that allow students to interact with people from outside their regular groups. This can help make sports a regular part of campus life rather than something students participate in only during major events.

I would also bring my interest in following and analyzing sports to the committee. I enjoy watching sports especially cricket and football. Understanding the strategy, decisions and the logic behind those decisions are something that makes me confident that I can excel at the Sports Committee. I would be happy to take responsibility for the execution of events, coordinate with participants, and ensure that activities are conducted smoothly and fairly. As a member of the Sports Committee, I hope to contribute with a positive attitude, willingness to take responsibility, and genuine enthusiasm for sports, while helping make the sporting experience at TAPMI more inclusive, active, and enjoyable for everyone.
favoriteMemory:
One of my favorite sports playing memories is from captaining a team in the Bhavan's Premier League, a leather-ball cricket tournament. In one of our matches, we lost two quick wickets with the team score still in single digits, putting us under pressure very early in the innings.

As captain, I felt the responsibility to step up and help the team recover. I came in and built a partnership with one of my friends, focusing on staying at the crease, rotating the strike, and rebuilding the innings rather than taking unnecessary risks. I scored 37 runs, and together we helped take the team from a difficult position to a competitive total and we eventually went on to win the match. That match remains one of my favorite sports memories because it showed me what I enjoy most about sports: the combination of responsibility, teamwork, and the ability to respond when things don't go according to plan The feeling of fighting back from a difficult start and eventually celebrating a win with the entire team is something I still remember fondly.

One of my favorite sports memories is watching Lionel Messi lift the FIFA World Cup in 2022. As someone who has followed football for years, seeing Messi finally win the biggest trophy in the sport was an incredibly special moment. What made the moment particularly special for me was what it represented for Messi. I had watched him for years and seen him come close to winning the World Cup in 2014, only to fall short. Seeing him finally lift the trophy after such a long wait felt like a personal joy

design.whyEvent: Being a staunch MS Dhoni fan, I am a big time believer that the process matters more than the results. I want to join the Event Coordinator Team because I enjoy being involved in the process of bringing an idea to life. While attending an event is the final experience, I find the process of planning and execution behind it equally interesting. From coordinating with different people to managing last-minute changes and making sure everything comes together smoothly, I believe the process itself can be both challenging and rewarding. I also see the Event Coordinator Team as an opportunity to interact with people across the campus and work with different teams. I enjoy working in groups and taking responsibility for getting things done, and I believe event coordination will help me contribute to the Committee with my skills.

name: Mann Patel
achievements: Played at the Zonal level in basketball during school and later captained my university basketball team, representing the university in multiple inter-college tournaments.
cultureAnswer:
My love for sports started when I began watching cricket matches with my dad after school. While watching, I still remember that I would always ask my dad how Sachin Tendulkar prepared for a match and what kind of strategies and discussions the team would have during the team huddle and Locker room. I was always curious to know what was happening behind the scenes while watching the match.

As I grew up, my passion for sports kept increasing. Every summer, I used to learn different sports at summer camps, and that's where I discovered my passion for basketball and eventually got selected for my school team.

I also started participating in and hosting local sports and Garba events in Ahmedabad. Later, I got a big opportunity to work with the Gujarat Titans during the 2025 IPL season as a contractual employee. My role involved on-ground marketing and managing ticket distribution for sponsors. From these experiences, I learned that a successful sports event is much more than what people see on match day. I learned how to coordinate within different departments and sponsors, understand sponsorship requirements, stay calm during last-minute surprises and unexpected challenges and Teamwork.

I have also worked on creating a sports infotainment project in VR, where users can experience the game from a player's perspective, bringing a new experience to sports infotainment. (You can check my project here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1b83oBZlj29UqwRwTq60l8eGtwJTIopKO) I have also worked on a sports app for SuperSport during my job. (Portfolio: https://mannportfolio2026.framer.website/projects/gamesense-supersport).

Therefore, for me, the Sports Committee is not about adding another position to my profile. It is about becoming part of something I genuinely love. Being involved in organizing crazy events like SPEED, Premiere Leagues also working with fellow sports enthusiasts, learning from their experiences, and contributing my own will be a great opportunity for me.

What I will contribute to the sports culture is my UX/UI design background, through which I can bring my design thinking, User experience design, and event management skills. Most importantly, I will bring my enthusiasm, positive energy, and team spirit to the committee.

#GameModeOn
favoriteMemory: My favorite memory was watching the live India vs. Netherlands match during the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup in Bengaluru. The stadium was packed with one of the craziest crowds I have ever experienced. Although it was an easy win for India, the real highlight for me was watching Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli play live. Hearing the entire stadium chant, "Kohli ko bowling do!", and then seeing him actually come on to bowl was an unforgettable moment. The best part was witnessing Virat Kohli take a wicket right in front of my eyes. The electrifying atmosphere and incredible vibe in the stadium made it a memory I'll never forget.

design.whyEvent: I come with experience in event coordination, whether it's organizing Garba events, sports events, or even fun family events like wedding functions. I always step up to take responsibility because I love working with team and different people, solving problems, handling the last-minute chaos that comes with every event and constantly think about unique ways to enhance the overall experience for everyone. At the end of successful planning and watch people having fun make me satisfied and happy and give confidence to take up the new task.

cultureAnswer: Being a part of the Sports Committee at TAPMI to me is much more than just pushing students to compete and participate in events, its about instilling the values of resilience, team work, and a strong sense of community that sports help you learn. I have grown up playing sports and it has been a crucial part of my personality development. Being a part of various individual and team sports events, I have learnt the importance of staying patient and showing perseverance, teamwork and focusing on good leadership skills under pressure , wherein my teammates and I are all striving towards the same goal. At TAPMI, I would love to make sporting events more encouraging, inclusive and engaging for everyone regardless of their skills. Mainly I believe in fostering a collaborative environment between the sports and other student committees to strengthen and prioritise campus spirit and bonding. Beyond event execution and coordination, I want to uplift the need of active participation, if students see sports as a means to build meaningful connections, grow, imbibe leadership skills and teamwork within themselves, this will create an extremely healthy balance amidst the demanding schedule and rigors of an MBA program. The idea numerous students have, that they need to know how to play sports and be good at it, needs to be changed for them to realise it is much more than being good at it , the learning outcomes and personality development is what they'll carry in the long run.
favoriteMemory:
My favourite sports memory while playing would always go back to the days wherein my dad would take the role of being my Badminton coach. name: MAHEK JHUNJHUNWALA
achievements:
Winner – Leo One Cricket Tournament.
Runner-up – Inter-College Cricket Tournament at iLEAD.
Active Cricket Player – Regularly participated in competitive cricket tournaments and team events.
cultureAnswer:
Being a part of the Sports Committee means much more to me than organizing tournaments, it means contributing to a culture that brings people together through passion, teamwork, and healthy competition. Sports have always been an important part of my life, teaching me discipline, resilience, and the value of working towards a common goal. I believe the Sports Committee has the unique opportunity to create experiences that become some of the most memorable moments of a student's MBA journey, and I would love to be a part of making those moments happen.

My experience at **Ballygunge Arena** gave me first-hand exposure to what goes into planning and executing successful sporting events. During my internship, I was involved in organizing the **Society Cricket League**, where I coordinated with teams, managed match schedules, ensured smooth communication, and handled on-ground execution. I also contributed to organizing a **two-day football tournament** and the **Racquet Nation Pickleball Tournament**. These experiences taught me that successful events are built on careful planning, teamwork, adaptability, and attention to detail. Whether it was coordinating participants, resolving last-minute challenges, or ensuring the event ran seamlessly, I learned how impactful efficient event management can be.

Alongside organizing sports events, I have always enjoyed participating in them. Winning the Leo One Cricket Tournament and finishing as the runner-up in the iLEAD Inter-College Cricket Tournament strengthened my confidence and reinforced the importance of perseverance, teamwork, and performing under pressure. These experiences have shaped my appreciation for sports, not just as competitions but as opportunities to learn, connect, and grow.

What excites me most about joining the Sports Committee is the opportunity to represent TAPMI. I want to be one of the girls who proudly wears the institute's jersey and competes in inter-college tournaments. While cricket has always been my primary sport, my passion has never been limited to it. I genuinely enjoy playing and learning different sports, whether it's basketball, badminton, squash, or any other game that challenges me physically and mentally. I believe every sport offers a new perspective and teaches valuable life lessons, and I want to make the most of every opportunity available at TAPMI.

If given the opportunity, I would contribute by helping organize well-executed tournaments while also encouraging greater participation across the student community. I want to help create an environment where students feel motivated to try new sports, support one another, and take pride in representing the institute. For me, being a part of the Sports Committee is about contributing both on and off the field, whether that's ensuring an event runs smoothly, cheering for my teammates, or striving to bring laurels to TAPMI. I hope to help build a sporting culture that is inclusive, energetic, and remembered long after our MBA journey comes to an end.
favoriteMemory:
My favorite sports memory is not just one match, it's following Virat Kohli's journey since the 2016 IPL season, when his record-breaking 973-run campaign made me an RCB fan for life. Over the years, I celebrated his iconic chases, centuries, and unwavering loyalty to RCB, but I also experienced the heartbreaks that came with supporting both him and the team. The toughest moment was watching India lose the 2023 ODI World Cup Final to Australia after an incredible unbeaten campaign. Like millions of fans, I was devastated, but Virat's resilience reminded me that setbacks are only temporary.

That is why watching India lift the 2024 T20 World Cup and, later, seeing RCB finally win their maiden IPL title in 2025 felt incredibly emotional. Watching Virat celebrate with tears in his eyes after years of dedication made the victory even more special. His journey has taught me that success isn't defined by never failing, but by continuing to believe, work hard, and rise stronger after every setback, a lesson that has stayed with me far beyond cricket.

design.whyEvent:
I want to join the Event Coordinator Team because I genuinely enjoy bringing people together through well-planned and engaging events. For me, the most rewarding part of any event is seeing months of planning come to life and creating an experience that participants remember long after it ends. I enjoy working in dynamic environments where every day presents a new challenge, and I find satisfaction in solving problems, coordinating with different stakeholders, and ensuring everything runs smoothly.

My previous experiences have given me the opportunity to understand event management from the ground up. As the Head of Mergers & Acquisitions for my college fest Invictus, I coordinated participants from multiple colleges, managed communication, and ensured the event was executed successfully. During my internship at Ballygunge Arena, I helped organize the Society Cricket League, the Racquet Nation Pickleball Tournament, and a two-day football tournament, where I handled coordination, scheduling, participant management, and on-ground execution. Being actively involved in the Leo Club of Calcutta Park Avenue further strengthened my planning and teamwork skills by organizing community initiatives and large-scale events.

At TAPMI, I want to contribute the same enthusiasm and commitment while learning from a team that sets high standards for campus events. I believe I can bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and a calm approach to handling pressure. More importantly, I want to be someone the team can rely on—whether it's brainstorming creative ideas, managing logistics, or stepping up when unexpected challenges arise. Joining the Event Coordinator Team would allow me to combine my passion for event management with my desire to create memorable experiences for the TAPMI community.

name: Hariprasad S
achievements: Runner-up at the ISC All Kerala Inter-School Football Championship (2017). Represented my school football team from 2017–19 and played for my college team across all three years, captaining the side in my final year.
cultureAnswer:
Sports has given me some of my closest, life-long friends and connections, and being part of the Sports Committee is my way of carrying that forward for others at TAPMI. To me, the committee isn't just about organizing games; it's about creating spaces where people bond, compete, and unwind from the academic grind.

I'd contribute by helping run flagship events like SPEED and Futsal, while also pushing for wider participation, not just among regular athletes, but among students who've never had a chance to play competitively. Having captained my college football team, I understand what it takes to build team spirit, keep people motivated, and get the logistics right. I'd bring that same energy to ensuring TAPMI's sports culture is inclusive, consistent, and something every batch looks forward to being part of.
favoriteMemory:
I've played plenty of inter-school and club matches over the years, but the one closest to my heart is my outgoing match in my final year of school, the traditional fixture where the 12th standard batch plays against the rest of the school.

It's a big deal. The whole school turns out to watch, and our batch was considered one of the strongest football sides our school had seen. From the whistle, we dominated. We controlled possession, created chance after chance, but somehow the goal just wouldn't come. As the clock wound down, the scoreline stayed frustratingly at 0-0.

With about five minutes left to play, the moment arrived. I got the ball outside the box, took my chance, and struck it. It flew in. The entire school erupted, chanting my name, and I still remember the wave of goosebumps that ran through me. It was pure, unfiltered joy, a core memory unlocked in an instant. We held on, and the match ended with us winning.

But the part that stayed with me came afterward. I freshened up and walked back into class, right in the middle of an ongoing period. The moment I stepped in, the whole class broke into applause. That second rush of goosebumps, the feeling of being celebrated by the people I'd spent years with, is something I'll never forget.

design.whyEvent: I want to join the Event Coordinator Team because I enjoy the work that goes on behind the scenes to bring people together, and I know how much a well-run event means to those taking part. I've done this before, as Head Coordinator of my school's Game Festival and by organizing an inter-college Futsal tournament for my college fest. Combined with captaining my college football team in my final year, these experiences taught me what it takes to manage logistics, lead a group, and stay calm when things don't go to plan. I want to help turn ideas into experiences people look forward to. I'm reliable, comfortable handling responsibility under pressure, and ready to put in the groundwork from early planning to the final whistle.

cultureAnswer:

favoriteMemory:
My favourite sports memory is watching the iconic India vs Pakistan match in the 2022 T20 World Cup on a big screen at the main road. I still remember the moment when India needed 28 runs from the last 8 balls with Virat Kohli at the crease. It was nearly impossible but what happened next became one of the best chases in the cricket history with Ashwin ending up the chase with a four.

The best part wasn't just the match, it was the people around me. Everyone watching was a stranger at first, but as India edged closer to victory, the place transformed. The moment India won, people were cheering, hugging each other, and celebrating together without even knowing each other's names. For those few minutes, nothing else mattered except the shared joy of witnessing something extraordinary.

Also the Jatin Sapru's passionate commentary made the experience even more memorable. That match reminded me that sports have a unique ability to unite people, create unforgettable emotions, and build connections beyond backgrounds or identities. That's the magic of sports, and it's a feeling I will always remember.

cultureAnswer:
For me being a part of the sports committee is more than organising the Tapmi flagship events like 'SPEED'. It's about building a community where students can relieve academic stress, learn teamwork, and grow outside the classroom. Sports naturally bring people together, and I see this committee as the heartbeat of student life. 

Fitness and sports have always been a core part of my life. As a former NCC Cadet Sergeant, my training in marksmanship and precision shooting taught me a lot about focus, patience, and staying calm under pressure. I also train regularly at the gym, focusing on weightlifting and complex movements like the clean and jerk. This routine has showed me that real results only come from consistency and hard work. I want to bring this same energy and mindset to TAPMI's sports culture. If I am selected, I plan to contribute in two main ways: running events smoothly and making sure everyone feels included.

First, I will use my professional and leadership experience to help manage our tournaments. Organizing a great sports event takes careful planning behind the scenes. In my role as an Administration Manager, I learned how to manage daily operations and coordinate teams effectively. I want to use these practical skills to make TAPMI’s sports fests even bigger and better organised.

Second, I want to make sure our sports culture includes everyone in the cohort. We should definitely have high-energy, competitive leagues for serious athletes, but we also need fun, casual events for beginners who just want to stay active and take a break from studying.

Overall, my goal is to combine my love for fitness with my hands-on management skills. I want to help create a sports culture at TAPMI that is fun, inclusive, and known for incredibly well-run events.
favoriteMemory:
If I had to pick my all-time favorite sports memory, it is easily the night of April 2, 2011.

Ever since I was a kid, I have always admired MS Dhoni not just as a cricketer, but as an individual and a leader. To me, he has always been "my captain," and I have the utmost respect for him. So, watching him hit that 2011 World Cup-winning six is a moment I will never forget. Just thinking about that swing of the bat and hearing the commentary, "Dhoni finishes off in style," still gives me goosebumps today.

What makes that memory so special to me isn't just the shot itself, but the mindset behind it. Deciding to promote himself up the batting order in the middle of a tense World Cup final took serious guts. He knew the stakes were incredibly high, and instead of passing the buck, he took the responsibility right on his own shoulders. That was a pure masterclass in leading from the front.

As someone who heavily values discipline and staying calm under pressure—lessons I picked up from my NCC days and use now while managing daily operations with my team—watching his absolute composure that night was incredibly inspiring. favoriteMemory:

Instead of giving up, we motivated each other, changed our approach, and focused on playing as a unit. The momentum shifted completely in the second half as we fought our way back into the game.

With the scores level and only a few minutes remaining, I found myself one-on-one with the goalkeeper. I managed to nutmeg the keeper and score the winning goal. The celebration that followed—with my teammates rushing over and the crowd cheering—is a moment I’ll never forget.

More than the goal itself, that match taught me the value of resilience, teamwork, and believing in each other even when the odds seem against you. It reinforced that success is built on collective effort, composure under pressure, and the confidence to seize opportunities when they arise.

That experience is one of the reasons I enjoy playing football, along with cricket and badminton. Every game is an opportunity to learn, compete, and grow, both as a player and as a person.

cultureAnswer:
Sports have always been much more than competition for me - they have shaped the way I think, work, and lead. From winning a district athletics medal and representing my school at the state level to later competing and winning an open bodybuilding championship, every phase of my sporting journey has taught me something different. Athletics taught me speed, discipline, and resilience under pressure, while bodybuilding taught me patience, consistency, and the importance of showing up every single day.
Being part of the Sports Committee would mean having the opportunity to create the same impact on others. I want sports at TAPMI to be something that every student feels comfortable participating in, whether they are competitive athletes or someone trying a sport for the first time.
My contribution would focus on participation as much as performance. Along with flagship tournaments, I would like to introduce beginner-friendly leagues, fitness challenges, inter-section competitions, and recreational events that encourage students from all backgrounds to get involved. The strongest sports culture is one where people play because they enjoy it, not only because they are competing for medals.
My four years of experience at Accenture has also strengthened my planning, coordination, and execution skills. Managing stakeholders, working with cross-functional teams, meeting deadlines, and solving problems under pressure are experiences I can bring to organizing sporting events efficiently.
I also believe fitness should become a year-round culture instead of something associated only with tournaments. Small initiatives such as morning runs, strength-training workshops, endurance challenges, or sports clinics conducted by experienced players can create sustained engagement across the campus.
If selected, my goal would be to help build a sporting culture where students compete fiercely, support each other wholeheartedly, and leave TAPMI with memories and friendships that extend far beyond the classroom.
favoriteMemory:
My favorite sports memory isn't the moment I stood on the podium with the gold medal - it was everything that happened before it.
In 2024, I was preparing for my first open bodybuilding competition. For over four and a half months, my life revolved around discipline. Every meal was measured, every workout was planned, and every day was spent in a calorie deficit while balancing a full-time corporate job. The preparation demanded consistency more than motivation.
Just when I entered the final phase of my preparation, I met with an accident. At that moment, I genuinely thought my competition was over. The injury made it impossible to train the way I normally would, and after investing months of effort, it was heartbreaking to think that everything might end there.
Three days later, I returned to the gym, not to lift heavy weights, but to do whatever my body could safely manage. I had only 20 days left before stepping on stage. Every session had to be adapted around my injury. Progress was slower, but giving up never felt like an option.
The final week was the toughest. Like most bodybuilding athletes before competition, I followed a strict peak week with virtually no carbohydrates, minimal sodium, and a carefully managed water cut. Going through that phase while recovering from an injury tested me physically and mentally in ways I had never experienced before.
When I finally stepped onto the stage, I wasn't thinking about the pain or the sacrifices. I was thinking about the months of preparation, the setbacks, and the decision to keep going when it would have been easier to quit. Hearing my name announced as the Gold Medal winner at the Arjun Shree of India Open Bodybuilding Championship made every challenge worthwhile.

achievements:
1. Represented my district panchkula in haryana state championship for 3 consecutive years, U-14 and U-16 which was conducted in compliance with the BCCI.
2. Represented Chandigarh in national private tournament.
3. gold medalist in inter school yoga competitions
4. Captain of my school cricket team.
cultureAnswer:
Sports have been a part of my life for as long as I can remember, and being a part of the Sports Committee would mean much more to me than simply organising tournaments. It would be an opportunity to contribute to something that has played a major role in shaping who I am today.

I started playing cricket at a young age and went on to represent Panchkula at the district level and Chandigarh at the U-19 level. While these achievements are important to me, I believe the biggest impact of sport has been on my personality. Cricket taught me discipline when I did not feel like training, resilience when things did not go my way and the importance of staying calm under pressure. It taught me that individual talent can only take you so far and that success often depends on how well you work with the people around you.

Many of the qualities I carry today have been shaped by my experiences in sports. Whether it is taking responsibility, working in a team, dealing with setbacks or stepping up when required, I often find myself drawing from the lessons I learnt on the field. Sports have also taught me that progress is rarely immediate. Improvement comes from consistently showing up, putting in the work and being willing to learn from both victories and failures. This mindset has shaped the way I approach challenges even outside sports.

At TAPMI, I would like to contribute towards building a sports culture that reflects this broader meaning of sport. I believe sports should not be limited to students who have played competitively or consider themselves athletes. A strong sports culture is one where everyone feels comfortable participating, whether they are competing seriously, playing casually with friends or trying a sport for the first time.

I would contribute by helping plan and execute well-organised, inclusive and engaging sporting events that encourage greater participation across the student community. I have experience in planning and organising events, and I understand the importance of coordination, communication, attention to detail and ensuring that things run smoothly on the ground. I would bring the same energy and commitment to organising sports activities at TAPMI.

More importantly, I want my peers to experience the positive impact that sports have had on my life. Sports have given me discipline, confidence, resilience, friendships and a sense of belonging. I would like to help create similar opportunities for my peers at TAPMI, regardless of their prior sporting experience. I believe sports can provide a much-needed break from academic pressures while also bringing people together and creating a stronger sense of community.

For me, being part of the Sports Committee would be a way of giving back to something that has given me so much. Sports have played a significant role in shaping who I am, and I would like to ensure that they can play a similar role in the lives of my peers. I would use my passion for sports and my experience in planning events to help build a sports culture at TAPMI that is competitive yet inclusive, ambitious yet enjoyable, and one that brings people together.
favoriteMemory:
This has to be one of my favourite questions because my favourite memory will always be from the cricket field.

Even today, when I think about that match, I can almost go back to that day. It was the final of an inter-school tournament, and we were playing against our arch-rivals. But what made the match even more special for me was that the other team had a player who had always been my counterpart. We had been competing against each other for years, even when we were both trying to make it into the state team. There was always this unspoken competition between us.

I remember dismissing him while I was bowling, and that already felt special. But the real battle began when we started batting. Our top order collapsed for very few runs, and I walked in when the team was under serious pressure. I still remember the feeling of walking out to bat. Somehow, as long as I was at the crease, I could sense a little fear in the opposition. I ended up hitting my counterpart for two sixes, and honestly, in that moment, it felt like I had won our personal battle.

There was also some good old sledging between me and the best bowler of their team, which made the whole match even more intense. But beneath all the excitement and the banter, I knew the situation was serious. It was the final, and after the batsman standing with me, there were only tailenders left. He played a crucial role by protecting his wicket, while I took responsibility for scoring the runs.

Together, we managed to take the team over the line, and we won the tournament. I was named Man of the Match in the final, and later, the achievement was announced in the school assembly. I remember feeling incredibly proud, but what I remember even more clearly is what my coach told me afterwards: “I was tension-free while you were batting.”

That sentence has stayed with me all these years. To me, it said more than any award could. It showed me the faith my coach had in me and the belief that I could handle the pressure when the team needed me most.

Even today, I find myself reminiscing about that match. I remember the rivalry, the pressure, the sledging, the two sixes, the partnership and the feeling of winning the final. But more than anything, I remember being a young cricketer who walked into a difficult situation and somehow managed to make it his day.

That match is a memory I will always hold close to my heart. Some moments stay with you long after the match is over, and for me, this is one of them.

My interest in event management comes from the experience I have gained by organising different kinds of events. I have been involved in organising HPS MUN 2023, which had around 250 delegates, and SD MUN 2024, which had around 120 delegates. I have also organised an Open Mic and a Bowling League. Organising these events taught me that a successful event requires much more than just a good idea. It requires detailed planning, coordination between multiple people, effective communication and the ability to remain calm when things do not go according to plan. I have enjoyed being involved in the entire process—from conceptualising and planning the event to coordinating with people and ensuring that things run smoothly on the day.

What I enjoy most about event management is seeing an idea transform into an actual experience for people. I like working behind the scenes, solving problems as they arise and making sure that the small details do not get overlooked. At the same time, organising events has taught me the importance of teamwork and adaptability because things rarely go exactly according to plan.

I want to join the Event Coordination Team because I believe my previous experience can help me contribute effectively while also allowing me to learn and take on greater responsibilities. More importantly, I want to be part of the team that creates experiences that students remember long after an event is over.

Having organised events ranging from MUNs to an Open Mic and a Bowling League, I have experienced different aspects of event management. I would like to build on that experience at TAPMI and contribute to making its events more organised, engaging and memorable.

name: Rachit Agarwala
otherSports: Apart from cricket, football, and tennis, I also follow Formula 1 and mixed martial arts (UFC).
cultureAnswer:
For me, sports has never been just a fitness routine or a competition to win, it's always felt like home. In the middle of case submissions, quizzes, and back-to-back deadlines, that one hour on the court or field is where I actually breathe. Being part of the Sports Committee, to me, means being the person who creates that same space for others, a place where people can forget about their pending assignments for a bit and just play.
At TAPMI, where the schedule barely gives you a moment to pause, I think sports culture shouldn't be an afterthought squeezed in between events, it should be something students look forward to every week. That's what I'd want to bring to the committee: consistency. Not just flagship tournaments once a semester, but small, regular touchpoints that keep the energy alive throughout the year.

Some things I'd want to work on:
1) A weekly "reset hour", a fixed 45 minutes to an hour, maybe on a weekday evening, where a different sport is arranged each week (badminton one week, football the next, cricket, table tennis, whatever the batch is up for). Nothing competitive, no pressure to perform, just students showing up, playing, and going back to their laptops feeling lighter.

2) Friendly matches across batches, sections, and cohorts, short, low-stakes games between MBA1 and MBA2, and across different sections and cohorts of the same batch, who otherwise rarely get a reason to interact outside classes.

3) Making sure equipment is actually accessible, a lot of participation drops not because people don't want to play, but because the shuttlecocks ran out, a ball is missing, or nobody knows what's available and when. I'd want the committee to track this properly, so equipment and courts are usable whenever someone wants to play, not just during scheduled events.

4) Making it inclusive, a lot of people stay away from sports at B-school because they feel "not good enough" or too out of practice. I'd want to make sure the committee's events are genuinely welcoming for someone picking up a racket after years, not just for the already-sporty crowd.

5) Using existing slots better, instead of only planning around big annual fests, tying up with the free hour students already have between classes, so sport becomes a habit, not an event.

6) Listening to feedback, a quick check-in after events or a simple way for students to tell us what sport they're missing, what timing doesn't work, or what's not being used, so decisions are based on what students actually want, not just what was done last year.

Beyond organizing, I think the committee's real job is to protect that feeling, the one where you step out of a stuffy classroom, get a game going, and for that half hour, nothing else exists except the ball, the score, and your friends laughing at you for missing an easy shot. If I'm part of this committee, that's the culture I'd want to build and protect, sports as the thing that keeps this campus sane, not just active.
favoriteMemory:
If you'd asked me this a few years ago, I probably would've talked about some football match or a tournament I played in. But honestly, my favorite sports memory isn't really one match, it's more of a feeling that's followed me since I was a kid.
My dad had a transferable job, so moving cities was just normal for us. And every time we moved, I was the new, thin kid again, trying to figure out a new school, new people, all of it. I was pretty introverted, so making friends never came easy. Sports ended up being the one thing that actually helped, every new city, it was the football ground or the coaching class where I ended up making friends first, way before I got comfortable talking to anyone in class.
I joined football coaching wherever we moved, and those one-hour sessions, twice a week, became something I actually looked forward to. Cities kept changing, faces kept changing, but that hour on the field stayed exactly the same, and I think that's why it meant so much, it was the one thing that felt mine no matter where we'd landed, and the fastest way I had of not feeling like an outsider anymore.
One memory that still stands out is going to a stadium to watch a match live for the first time. I don't even remember the score properly anymore, but I remember screaming with a stadium full of strangers like we'd known each other for years and waking up the next morning with my throat completely sore from all the cheering. It's such a small, stupid thing to remember, but it's stayed with me longer than most of the actual match.
But if I had to pick just one memory, it wouldn't be from the field or the stadium at all. It would be watching cricket with my family, especially my dad. Late nights, arguing over umpiring decisions, getting far too worked up over a game neither of us could control. At the time it just felt like a normal night. I didn't think of it as anything special.
It's only now, being away from home, that I realize how much I miss exactly that, not the game itself, but sitting there with him, half-watching, half-arguing, completely forgetting about everything else going on in my life.
Even now, every time there's a big match, I end up calling him. We spend more time arguing about a shot or a decision than actually discussing the score. And somehow those calls make me feel closer to home than most conversations do.
The nights I remember most are the ones that went on till 2 a.m., nobody asking about marks, nobody asking what's next. Just the two of us, completely caught up in a game that meant nothing and everything at the same time.
That's why this stays my favorite sports memory. Not because of anything I won or achieved, but because sport was always quietly there, in every new city, in every awkward first week, in the background of the moments that actually mattered to me.

design.whyEvent:

In college, I was part of a committee for two years, and most of what I did was being on ground, making sure things were actually happening the way they were supposed to, catching the small things before they became problems, and stepping in wherever something needed sorting. I liked that. Watching an event go from a rough idea to actually happening, smoothly, because someone was there making sure it did, that's satisfying in a way I didn't expect.
On top of that, in my work experience, I've collaborated closely with cross-functional teams, people with different priorities, different working styles, and had to get everyone aligned on a deadline anyway. That taught me coordination isn't just assigning tasks, it's clear communication and being someone people can actually rely on when things get chaotic.
I think that mix, hands-on event experience plus working in team setups professionally, is what I'd bring here. I'm not looking to just sit in meetings and pitch ideas; I want to be the person actually on ground making sure everything runs smoothly, because that's genuinely the part I'm good at.

cultureAnswer:
For me, sports are much more than competition, they are a way of building character, discipline, and mental strength. I truly believe that sports played a major role in shaping the person I am today.

Until Class 7, I was an average student with limited confidence. Everything changed when I started playing sports. The discipline of training, the responsibility of being part of a team, and the confidence gained through competition positively influenced every aspect of my life. My academic performance improved, I became more confident, and I learned how to handle pressure and setbacks. Looking back, sports gave me lessons that extended far beyond the playing field.

An MBA is an intense journey filled with academic pressure, deadlines, and constant competition. I believe that regular participation in sports helps students maintain both their physical fitness and mental well-being. It provides an opportunity to refresh, connect with peers, and develop qualities such as teamwork, leadership, resilience, and decision-making.

If I become a part of the Sports Committee, my focus would be on making sports more accessible and inclusive for everyone, regardless of their skill level. I would encourage regular tournaments, friendly matches, fitness challenges, and recreational sporting events that motivate students to participate without hesitation. I also want to create an environment where students feel comfortable trying new sports and building friendships through shared experiences.

Having served as the captain of my school’s football and athletics teams, I understand the importance of planning, coordination, and motivating people towards a common goal. I would bring the same enthusiasm, responsibility, and teamwork to TAPMI’s Sports Committee and work towards creating a vibrant sporting culture that encourages participation, promotes well-being, and strengthens the campus community.
favoriteMemory:
My favorite sports memory is winning the Kerala Gramolsavam Football Tournament this year with my local club.

Before the tournament, we were certainly not considered favourites. Most of our players were experienced but had been away from regular practice for quite some time. On paper, other teams looked stronger. However, what we lacked in match fitness, we made up for with determination, trust, and exceptional team spirit. Every player was committed to giving their best, and that unity became our biggest strength throughout the tournament.

The final was an unforgettable experience. After a closely contested match, the game went to a penalty shootout. Although I normally play as a left wing-back, I stepped in as the goalkeeper for the shootout. I managed to save two penalties, and those saves ultimately helped our team lift the trophy.

What made that moment even more special was the realization that nearly ten years earlier, during my school football days, I had trained as a goalkeeper specifically for penalty shootout situations. Even though I eventually became a defensive outfield player, those lessons stayed with me. A decade later, that training unexpectedly became the reason our team won the championship.

That experience reinforced a lesson I carry with me in every aspect of life: no sincere effort or learning ever goes to waste. The hard work we put in today may not reward us immediately, but it often returns when we least expect it. That victory will always remind me of the value of preparation, perseverance, and believing in your team, even when others don’t.

cultureAnswer:
Being part of the Sports Committee isn't just about managing schedules or setting up equipment it’s about creating a culture where sports serve as a powerful outlet, a community builder, and a driver of well-being on campus.
At a high-intensity B-school like TAPMI, where academic rigor and tight deadlines are the norm, sports are essential. To me, the committee’s role is to ensure every student whether they're a seasoned athlete competing in inter-college tournaments or someone looking for a stress-relieving casual game finds a welcoming, well-organized space to engage.
Here is how I plan to contribute to building and strengthening that s
ports culture at TAPMI:
1. Inclusivity Beyond Core Tournaments
While major events like the TAPMI Premier League (TPL) and inter-batch sports bring high energy, a sustainable sports culture requires continuous, accessible engagement.
•	Intramural "Flash Leagues": Introduce quick, weekend mini-tournaments (e.g., 3v3 basketball, futsal, or badminton doubles) designed for low time commitment so busy students can easily participate.
•	Beginner & Casual Sessions: Host periodic non-competitive pickup sessions or beginner workshops to encourage students who might feel intimidated by competitive trials to stay active.
2. Operational Rigor & Player Experience
A strong sports culture relies on reliable execution. If events run smoothly, participation and enthusiasm naturally follow.
•	Structured Timelines: Publish event calendars well in advance so students can balance academics, committee work, and sports without last-minute scheduling conflicts.
•	Inventory & Facility Management: Ensure equipment is well-maintained, facilities are organized, and booking/access systems are seamless and fair for all batches.
3. Community Building & Mental Well-being
Sports are one of the fastest ways to break down silos between batches, sections, and programs.
•	Inter-Batch Camaraderie: Design events specifically structured to pair junior and senior batches together, using sports as an informal networking and mentorship bridge.
•	Wellness & Fitness Integration: Collaborate with wellness initiatives on campus to promote fitness, strain recovery, and mental health through active physical routines.
favoriteMemory:
Watching:

The match took place on March 8, 2017, when FC Barcelona hosted Paris Saint-Germain at the Camp Nou for the second leg of the UEFA Champions League Round of 16. Three weeks prior, PSG had stunned the footballing world by thrashing Barcelona 4–0 in Paris, leaving the Spanish giants needing a minimum five-goal victory to advance. Up to that point in Champions League history, no team had ever successfully overturned a four-goal first-leg deficit. The match was widely expected to be a routine night of qualification for Paris, but it quickly transformed into the ultimate stage for an unprecedented comeback, forever etched into football lore as La Remontada ("The Comeback").
What made the game legendary was not just the victory itself, but the sheer emotional rollercoaster and sheer impossibility of how it unfolded. Barcelona set the tone early with intense pressing, going up 3–0 by the 50th minute thanks to goals from Luis Suárez, Layvin Kurzawa own goal, and a Lionel Messi penalty. However, disaster struck in the 62nd minute when PSG’s Edinson Cavani smashed home an away goal. Under the away-goals rule at the time, this meant Barcelona’s 3–0 lead on the night was no longer enough; they now needed three more goals without reply to avoid elimination, leaving them stranded at 3–1 (3–5 on aggregate) as the clock ticked down.
With only two minutes of regulation time remaining, the task seemed entirely out of reach. What followed was seven minutes of pure bedlam led by a masterclass performance from Neymar Jr. In the 88th minute, Neymar curled a phenomenal free-kick into the top corner, and just three minutes later, he calmly converted a penalty to make it 5–1 on the night. Tying the aggregate score at 5–5 was still not enough due to PSG's away goal, meaning Barcelona needed one last miracle in stoppage time. In the 95th minute, with even goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen up in the opposition half, Neymar floated a delicate chip into the penalty box. Substitute Sergi Roberto lunged forward, stretching to volley the ball past Kevin Trapp into the back of the net to seal a miraculous 6–1 win (6–5 aggregate), sending the Camp Nou into absolute euphoria and delivering the greatest comeback in the history of the sport.

Playing

It happened when I was in 10th and participating in K M Munshi Memorial Athletic Meet ( A sports meet for mainly Kochi based CBSE schools). It happened during a 4x100m relay race. I had 100m prelims and 800m prelims in the morning and finals for both in the noon. By the time the relay races started I was too tired to even stand. Everything that happened afterwards where a blur.
I remember receiving the baton and screaming my lungs out. When I came back to my senses we had won the race and apparently I had been screaming the entire time I ran. It was the single most tiresome and exhilarating sports moment of my life.

For me, being a part of the Sports Committee is much more than organizing tournaments, it's about creating a culture where sports become an integral part of campus life. Sports have shaped my personality by teaching me discipline, teamwork, resilience, and leadership and I want every student at TAPMI to experience those values.
Having represented my university at the West Zone level and having served as the Head of the Sports Committee during my undergraduate studies, I understand both the player's and organizer's perspective. These experiences have taught me how to coordinate events, manage teams, solve problems under pressure, and ensure smooth execution.
If selected, I would focus on increasing participation by organizing beginner-friendly tournaments, inter-section leagues, and fun sports events that encourage students of all skill levels to take part. I would also introduce 1-minute classroom sports challenges such as paper-basketball, cup stacking, reaction-time games, balance challenges, and sports trivia. These activities require minimal resources, can be conducted during short breaks, and would encourage participation from both students and faculty, making sports a part of everyday campus life rather than just scheduled tournaments.
Additionally, I would work towards maintaining transparent team selection processes, better communication of schedules, and creating a supportive environment where competitive athletes and recreational players feel equally valued.
I believe a strong sports culture is built not only by winning tournaments but by fostering participation, inclusivity, and team spirit. I would be committed to making sports a platform that brings the TAPMI community together while proudly representing the institute in external competitions.
favoriteMemory:
If I had to pick one sports memory that I'll always cherish, it would be captaining my SEMCOM cricket team to the championship. Walking onto the field as captain, knowing that the entire team trusted my decisions, was a feeling I'll never forget. Every match brought a different challenge, but we stayed united, backed each other, and eventually lifted the trophy together. The icing on the cake was being awarded the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the tournament. Winning as a team while also contributing individually made that moment incredibly special.

Another memory that is equally close to my heart is winning back-to-back badminton titles for SEMCOM. Defending the title was even more satisfying because it reflected consistency, discipline, and the countless hours spent practicing.
Whenever I look back, I don't just remember the trophies , I remember the team huddles before matches, the celebrations after every win, and the friendships built through sports. Those moments taught me that sports are not just about winning; they're about creating memories, building character, and sharing experiences that stay with you for life.

name: Aastha Satakshi
achievements: I have represented my state three times in gymnastics at the state level during my school years. Recently, I also took up Taekwondo as a hobby, and it has become an important part of my life.
cultureAnswer:
Before telling why I want to be a part of the Sports Committee, I want to answer why sports? I was in 6th standard when I was introduced to sports for the first time. Initially, I thought it was all about winning medals but as I grew up, I realised it was never really about the sport. It was about the people you meet because of it. It was about the friendships that happen without trying, the bond you build after every practice, the support you get from your friends and the discipline and consistency that slowly become a part of who you are. Sports have given me some of my best memories, but more importantly, they have always helped me find myself again. There was a phase when academics took over, then college happened, then work happened. Somewhere in between, sports took a backseat. During CAT preparation, everything felt overwhelming. There were days when I felt mentally exhausted and questioned myself a lot. After my exams, I joined Taekwondo, and I still remember thinking after one practice session, “I had missed this so much.” It wasn’t because I had become good at Taekwondo overnight. It was because, for that two hour, I wasn’t thinking about CAT, placements, or what was going to happen next. I was just…there. That’s why I want to be a part of the Sports Committee.

For me, it isn’t just about organising events. It’s about creating more of those moments for people. MBA is hectic. Everyone is chasing deadlines, quizzes, internships and placements. I want sports to become that one thing people look forward to every once in a while, not because they have to come, but because they genuinely want to.

I'd love to create smaller, more casual activities. Maybe before every third Saturday we could float a Google Form and whoever wants to join can come to the beach for a game of volleyball, frisbee, or even just fun games. Another idea is a Run-Fun Sunday, where people come together for a morning run followed by breakfast. No competition. No pressure. Just people spending time together.
favoriteMemory:
My favourite sports memory is actually a very recent one from Taekwondo.

I had joined Taekwondo only three months before our district tournament, but in those three months, I met people I know I’m going to keep in my life forever. We practised together, went out to eat together, shared our worries, fought with each other, but one thing we all knew was that no one was giving up on anyone. We were stuck together for life. We celebrated each other’s progress, pushed each other during practice, and somewhere along the way, we started feeling like a family.

Then came the day of the tournament, and it wasn’t easy. The schedule wasn’t managed properly, so our team had been waiting from morning till evening. The match got delayed by almost 12 hours, and by the time my friend Isha was called for her fight, she was exhausted and had fallen quite sick. Looking at her, all of us were genuinely worried.

What happened next is something I’ll never forget.

The moment Isha stepped into the arena, Muskan started cheering. And when I say cheering, I mean she was literally screaming at the top of her lungs. Every single kick, every point, every second of that fight, she kept shouting Isha’s name with so much energy and belief that I still get goosebumps thinking about it. I’ve seen people cheer before, but this was different. It wasn’t just cheering, it was as if Muskan had decided that there was no way she was going to let Isha lose. The way she was cheering, the way she wanted Isha to win so badly, it was something I’ll never forget. Somewhere in that moment, I realised how powerful it is to have someone who believes in you even when you’re exhausted, scared, or not at your best. The thing that stayed with me was watching one person believe in another so fiercely that it gave me goosebumps. That day made me realise that sports are so much more than medals. Sometimes, they’re about knowing that someone has your back so completely that they simply refuse to let you give up.

And I think everyone deserves a Muskan in their life.

name: Siddhi Kambli
cultureAnswer:
Sport has been part of my life for as long as I can remember, purely out of love for it. I've tried many outdoor sports, with lawn tennis as my longest stint at about 10+ years. This led me straight to my first job: what started as an internship at The Sports Gurukul turned into a full-time role spanning operations, events, admissions, and sports coaching.

On the events side, I was part of the team that executed the Elpro Sports Fest - a 10-day multi-sport event in Pune for over 5,000 school students, and the Schoolathon, a half-marathon in Mumbai with 3,000+ participants among others. Both events meant coordinating large volunteer teams, managing schedules and venues, tracking budgets, and staying on top of safety protocols for thousands of participants across age groups. These align closely with what this role demands. I also coached toddlers under the Ready Steady Go Kids program, a different but equally valuable side of working with people in sport.

I dislocated my shoulder last year and haven't been able to play anything long-term since. I've been rehabbing it, but I haven’t been able to get back to sports yet. That's part of why the Sports Committee feels like the right fit: it lets me stay close to sports.

As Event Coordinator, I'd focus on:
- Planning and running events meticulously, following clear timelines and maintaining defined ownership
- Coordinating volunteers and team members, since managing events taught me how to delegate clearly and keep a large team aligned on event day
- Managing budgets and logistics for venues, equipment, schedules 
- Collecting feedback throughout and making sure to analyse what went wrong and how it can be fixed/made better for the next event
favoriteMemory:
I can’t describe it as a single memory, but more like a feeling that I miss - just being on a tennis court. Once I stepped on, I'd lose all track of time. Hours would go by without me noticing. My parents eventually stopped asking where I was; they knew that once I went to play, there was no telling when I'd be back. They would just call to check when I was coming home.
That feeling of losing all sense of time is something I still miss, and part of why I want to stay close to sport even now, through something like the Sports Committee.

design.whyEvent: I want to be part of the team that actually makes the kind of events happen where people pour their heart into it. Working on the Elpro Sports Fest and the Schoolathon taught me that it takes good scheduling, keeping volunteers on the same page, and staying calm when things don't go to plan. But honestly, what I love most is that feeling when it all comes together; months of planning finally playing out, imperfect but real. I want to chase that again - the adrenaline during and the dopamine hit after - with the Sports Committee.

favoriteMemory:
I was at the Taekwondo National Championship in Bangalore. I looked at the fixture, thought "the history is going to repeat itself".
I have always been a little short for Taekwondo. But this time, everyone in my category was much taller than me. I was barely reaching their shoulders. To make things worse my first fight was against someone from Bangalore. I knew I had to win really big a small win was not going to be enough.
I was worried but I do not know what got into me once I heard the whistle, I just started fighting. I won that first fight by 25 Points. I won the next two fights by knockouts. Then in my 4th bout I was fighting one of the tallest girls in the category I did a jumping kick and ended up twisting my ankle, I won that fight. By the time the bronze medal match came around, my ankle was shot. Everyone told me to call it quits, but I had total Karate Kid energy going on, there was no way I was backing down. I limped back out onto the mat and fought with everything I had left. I ended up losing that final match, but I walked away with my head held high.
I didn't win the bronze, but that tournament is still my favorite memory. It proved to me that height and odds don't mean much when you've got the heart, and a little bit of stubbornness!

cultureAnswer:

favoriteMemory:
My favorite recent sports memory is the intense ending of the 2024 FIDE Candidates Chess Tournament. Even though 17-year-old D. Gukesh made history as the youngest World Championship challenger, what I remember most is what happened right after the final-round game between Fabiano Caruana and Ian Nepomniachtchi.

Before the last round, both Caruana and Nepomniachtchi knew they had to win to catch up with Gukesh and force a tiebreak. The game turned into a tough, 109-move battle. Caruana got close to winning and gave it everything he had, but as the clock ran down, he lost his advantage. The game ended in a draw, which meant both players were out and Gukesh became the winner.

What stood out most was not the chessboard, but the emotion after the game. Caruana, clearly heartbroken after losing his chance at the World Championship, turned to Nepomniachtchi and apologized. In that moment, even though he was deeply disappointed, Caruana realized that missing the win also ended his opponent’s hopes.

This memory stands out to me because it shows both the inspiring and harsh sides of sports. There was the amazing rise of a young prodigy, and at the same time, the tough loss for experienced players who gave it their all. Caruana’s apology was a real moment of sportsmanship and humanity, proving that even in the most intense competitions, there is a quiet understanding between rivals.

favoriteMemory:
My favorite sports memory is from the High Jump final in 12th grade — and it's not because I won, but because of everything that happened before that.

It came down to me and one other competitor. We were neck and neck, clearing height after height, and the tension kept building with every round. Coming into the second-last height, he cleared it on his second attempt. Then it was my turn — and on my second attempt, I twisted my ankle mid-jump. For a second, I genuinely thought that was it — that my competition was over, right there.

But I didn't want to walk away like that. I went for my third and final attempt on that same height, pushed through the pain, and cleared it. The moment I landed, the entire crowd — my fellow students — just erupted. That reaction is something I'll never forget; it wasn't even the final result yet, but the sheer will to get over that bar with a twisted ankle earned the loudest reaction I'd ever gotten in any competition.

Neither of us could clear the next height after that, so the placings came down to that second-last round — he'd cleared it in his second attempt, and I'd cleared it in my third. So he finished first, and I finished second.

I didn't get the gold that day, but that memory has stuck with me more than any medal I've won. It taught me something I carry with me even now — that pushing through when things go wrong, even when you think it's over, is worth more than the result itself. That's the kind of spirit I'd want to bring into any team or committee I'm part of.

design.whyEvent:
I want to apply for Event Coordinator because it's the role that matches how I've naturally operated my whole life someone who doesn't just show up to play, but ends up organizing, leading, and making sure things run right. As captain of my football team, I wasn't just leading during the match I was coordinating practice schedules, resolving conflicts within the team, and making sure everyone showed up prepared. That same instinct is what draws me to this role turning an idea for a sports event into something that actually happens smoothly, on time, and without chaos.

I'm also someone who stays composed when things go wrong like that high jump final where I twisted my ankle mid-competition and still had to make a call in the moment. Event coordination is full of those moments last-minute changes, scheduling clashes, a ground booking falling through and I'd rather be the person solving that problem in real time than watching from the sidelines.

On top of that, I'm currently SPOC for fundraising at Samnidhy, TAPMI's student-managed fund, where I directly coordinate with stakeholders and manage deliverables under deadlines. That experience has already given me a taste of what real event/coordination responsibility feels like, and I want to bring that same ownership to sports events specifically, because sports is where my passion genuinely lies.

name: Akash Kumar Jha
cultureAnswer:
Being a person who once played a lot of sports, whether passionately or just as a hobby, the sports committee is like a home for me. Being a part of the Sports Committee means much more to me than organizing tournaments. It means creating an environment where it's not just about playing sports; it's way more than that. It's about bringing people together, encouraging healthy competition, and giving everyone a chance to unwind from the demanding MBA schedule.
I've always believed that sports are one of the best ways to teach yourself values like resilience, teamwork, discipline, and handling both victory and defeat with grace. I want to contribute to a culture where participation is valued just as much as winning, making every student feel welcome regardless of their skill level. Every person who takes part I should enjoy and fall in love with the whole process of being in a competitive tournament-like atmosphere like I fell in 8th standard.
If selected, I would contribute by ensuring events are well-planned, inclusive, and engaging. From coordinating fixtures and logistics to managing volunteers and handling last-minute challenges, I would take ownership to ensure every event runs smoothly. Beyond execution, I would also focus on increasing participation through inter-section challenges, beginner-friendly tournaments, and fun recreational events (still have to think about what those activities could be, but if given enough time, I can think of a few really good ideas or so) that encourage even non-athletes to step onto the field.
I also believe feedback is essential. After every event, I would gather suggestions from participants to continuously improve the experience and make future events even better. See, because sports will remain the same, but the whole vibe or experience of even watching them holds great value. So the feedback is important.
Most importantly, I want SportsCom to be remembered not just for hosting competitions but for building a campus where students look forward to playing, supporting their peers, and celebrating sports together. If I can help create that sense of enthusiasm and belonging, I would consider my contribution a success.
favoriteMemory: My favorite sports memory would be me playing for the district tournament for basketball, representing my school, Central Academy, back when I was in 8th grade. For me, why this is such a special memory is because it was the first time my parents allowed me to play and participate in any non-academic activity, especially sports activities. I knew I had to show my best result to carry on this sports journey; hence, I have to perform the best that I can. But then again, our district tournament started; in the first match, we got a BYE for our team. In the second match we barely won; it was a knockout tournament, and we knew we were underprepared. I knew I could have practiced more and more and more. But it was too late to regret. After all the close calls, we reached the finals. But in that final we lost really bad; I still remember our score was 18 and the other team scored 42. It was the worst we could have played or the worst we could have hoped to happen. Our morale was down; it was the first time for all of us to take part in such tournaments. Even though it was just a district match, we put in a lot of effort. In return, we reached the finals; we did our best, yet we didn't get what we wanted till the end. My sports teacher, she herself dropped me at my home, and I remember her telling me to keep my chin up by telling me those words, which I still value a lot: "Aakash, losing in the start is necessary; it teaches you the value of winning, it teaches you the value of trying harder, it teaches you why you shouldn't quit, and also it teaches you to stay humble no matter how good you get at anything. Every missed layup today will affect you more than those 1000 layups successfully done by you in practice matches. Trying never stops; you have to keep your chin high no matter the outcome." I play basketball now as a leisure activity, not as a passion, but the lesson from that single district tournament has taught me a lot of things, a lot of things I still value in my life and will in the future too.

favoriteMemory:
As a Messi fan since my 2nd Grade, I had followed his journey for years the moments of brilliance, the heartbreak of losing the 2014 World Cup final, and the criticism he faced despite winning almost everything at the club level. Many believed he would never win the one trophy that mattered most to him.
The 2022 World Cup felt different. Every match carried immense pressure, and Messi consistently stepped up when his team needed him the most. Watching Argentina overcome setbacks, fight through difficult matches, and eventually reach the final was an emotional journey in itself.
The final against France is in my opinion, one of the greatest football matches ever played. There were moments when it seemed Argentina had won, only for France to fight back. The game kept everyone on the edge of their seats until the penalty shootout. When Gonzalo Montiel scored the winning penalty and Messi dropped to his knees in celebration, I couldn't hold back my emotions. Me and my friends had tears of joy because it felt like years of perseverance, sacrifice, and belief had finally been rewarded.
What made that moment special wasn't just the trophy it was the lesson behind it. Messi's career taught me that setbacks don't define you. Despite losing major finals and facing constant criticism, he never gave up, never stopped improving, and continued leading by example. His resilience and humility are qualities I deeply admire.
That memory continues to inspire me beyond sports. Whenever I face challenges, I remind myself that success often comes after persistence, patience, and consistent effort. Messi's World Cup victory reinforced my belief that if you keep working hard and never lose faith in your goal, setbacks become part of the journey rather than the end of it.
For me, that night wasn't just about Argentina becoming world champions it was about witnessing one of the greatest examples of determination and the rewards of never giving up.

cultureAnswer:
Being part of the Sports Committee, to me, is about ensuring that every student who wants to play a sport gets the opportunity to do so. Sports have shaped a large part of my journey at TAPMI as the Sports Representative, SPEED Captain, and then Captain of the Women's Basketball Team, but they've also shown me where we can do better.

favoriteMemory:
My favourite sports memory is surprisingly not winning a match or lifting a trophy. It happened during the closing ceremony of SPEED'25.

As the ceremony was coming to an end, the names of the captains for the upcoming Inter-MAHE teams were being announced. I was simply sitting in the audience, applauding for everyone else, with absolutely no expectation of hearing my own name. Then, suddenly, I was called on stage as the Captain of the TAPMI Women's Basketball Team for 2025.

For a few seconds, I genuinely couldn't process what had happened. I wasn't prepared for it, and I definitely wasn't expecting it. Walking up to the stage, I felt a mix of surprise, pride, excitement, and responsibility all at once. It's my favourite sports memory because it was completely unexpected, and that's what made it so special. Even today, whenever I think about it, I remember the feeling of hearing my name and realising that I had been entrusted with something much bigger than myself.

achievements:

and was honored with the Maharana Mewar Fateh Singh Award for Excellence in Chess
